sections.title: Basic Concept of Statement and Assumption
sections.content: A Statement is a sentence that expresses a fact, decision, suggestion, or piece of information. An Assumption is a hidden idea that the speaker takes for granted without stating it directly. In competitive exams, the task is to identify which unstated idea is automatically assumed behind the given statement.

sections.title: Simple Method to Identify Assumptions
sections.content: Whenever a person says something, they already consider certain things to be true. These unstated beliefs are assumptions. If this hidden idea turns out to be false, the statement becomes weak. Therefore, it is important to find the unstated idea that is necessary for the statement.

sections.title: Cause and Effect Assumptions
sections.content: When a step is suggested to solve a problem, it is assumed that the step will actually help reduce or solve the problem. Example: If a signboard says 'Do not throw garbage here', it assumes that people will read the sign and avoid throwing garbage.

sections.title: Advertisement Assumptions
sections.content: When a product is advertised, it is assumed that people are interested in that product and have the ability to buy it. For example, if a company advertises a new mobile phone, it assumes that customers may want to purchase it.

sections.title: Advice Assumptions
sections.content: When someone gives advice, it is assumed that the listener is willing to consider the advice and may follow it. Example: If a teacher advises a student to practice daily, it assumes that the student values the advice and may act on it.

sections.title: 2–3 Step Logical Evaluation Method
sections.content: Step 1: Carefully read the statement and understand its meaning. Step 2: Think about what the speaker has assumed to be true without saying it. Step 3: Check whether the statement would become weak if that hidden idea were false. If yes, then it is the correct assumption.

sections.title: Difference Between Related Thought and Assumption
sections.content: Not every related idea is an assumption. An assumption is something that must be true for the statement to make sense. If an option only provides general information but does not affect the statement, it should not be considered an assumption.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Students often treat general knowledge as an assumption. 2. Repeating information already given in the statement. 3. Thinking too far beyond the statement and selecting ideas not directly connected to it.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: A Statement is what is said, while an Assumption is what is implied but not stated. The correct assumption is the one that must be true for the statement to hold. In cases of cause-effect, advertisement, and advice, assumptions usually relate to human behavior or response.

tricks.title: Necessary vs Extra Idea Trick
tricks.explanation: An assumption must be necessary for the statement. If it is false, the statement becomes weak.
tricks.example: Statement: The government placed warning boards to stop smoking. Assumption: People read the boards.

tricks.title: Negative Test Trick
tricks.explanation: Reverse the assumption. If the statement collapses, the assumption is correct.
tricks.example: If people do not read the boards, placing warning boards becomes useless.

tricks.title: Advice Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: When advice is given, it is assumed the listener can hear and possibly follow the advice.
tricks.example: Statement: The doctor advised the patient to exercise daily. Assumption: The patient may follow the doctor's advice.

tricks.title: Advertisement Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: Advertising assumes that people may be interested in buying the product.
tricks.example: Statement: The company advertised a new phone. Assumption: People may want to buy the phone.

tricks.title: Cause and Effect Trick
tricks.explanation: If an action is taken, it assumes that the action will help solve the problem.
tricks.example: Statement: The school installed CCTV cameras to improve discipline. Assumption: Cameras will improve discipline.

tricks.title: Repeat Statement Identification
tricks.explanation: If an option simply repeats the statement, it is not an assumption.
tricks.example: Statement: Traffic in the city has increased. Option: The number of vehicles has increased. This is just a related thought.

tricks.title: Common Sense Trap Trick
tricks.explanation: Not every common idea is an assumption. Only necessary ideas count.
tricks.example: Statement: The library will remain open late. Assumption: Students may come to study.

tricks.title: Hidden Link Trick
tricks.explanation: The hidden connection between the action and the expected result is the assumption.
tricks.example: Statement: The company reduced prices to increase sales. Assumption: Lower prices increase sales.

tricks.title: Behavior-Based Trick
tricks.explanation: Many assumptions are based on expected human behavior.
tricks.example: Statement: A speed limit board was installed on the road. Assumption: Drivers will slow down after seeing it.

tricks.title: Direct Relation Trick
tricks.explanation: The correct assumption must be directly connected to the statement.
tricks.example: Statement: The school started a new bus service. Assumption: Some students need transportation.
